Date: 2026-10-21
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Iris), Marcus Chu (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Head of Security), Alex Gomez (Product)
summary: Discovery call: Iris Health exploring migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated or Private. Primary drivers: cost predictability at scale, data residency/SOC2 requirements, and achieving eval parity (latency and quality) when moving from OpenAI + vLLM internal stack. Discussed architecture, compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI model formats, tokenization), benchmark plan, and next steps to run a 1-week pilot on Dedicated capacity.
topics: Current stack: OpenAI + internal vLLM serving for burst/edge use
Compatibility: TGI/vLLM model weights and tokenizer parity
Performance: latency SLOs and KV cache behavior
Cost/TCO: per-token vs reserved Dedicated pricing
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Jonah our SE is here too. Quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: Hi, Lena here, CTO at Iris. We've been running majority on OpenAI for prod with some internal vLLM nodes for burst and offline evals.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus, ML Eng -- we handle model infra and the vLLM stack.
[00:23] Priya: Priya, security. Looking at compliance and data flow.
[00:28] Jonah: Great, thanks. High level what's motivating the migration?
[00:34] Lena: Two things: predictable cost and data residency. OpenAI's fine for early stage, but at our volumes it's getting expensive and we need stronger audit logs and a private option for PHI-ish data. Also, we noticed some quality drift when switching between OpenAI hosted versions and our vLLM replicas.
[00:50] Maya: Totally makes sense. We see a lot of customers in that spot. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools plus the option for a Private VPC control plane. For the eval parity point, can you explain your vLLM workflow?
[01:05] Marcus: Sure. We use TGI-compatible weights pulled from checkpoints, run them on vLLM for low-latency serving. Tokenization is a bit custom in places; sometimes outputs differ from OpenAI verbatim, especially around function-calling and stop sequences. We want to make sure when we move to Redwood the outputs match our acceptance tests.
[01:24] Jonah: Understood. On compatibility: Redwood supports standard HF model formats as well as TGI variants in many cases. There are subtle differences in tokenization and sampling defaults — we'll document those and we can run identical warmup runs. Also our runtime handles KV cache similarly but implementation-level differences can affect latency at long context lengths.
[01:45] Lena: How about vLLM? Our ops team uses vLLM for cost efficiency at certain loads — can Redwood Dedicated integrate or replace that?
[01:55] Jonah: You can do either. For many customers we replace vLLM with our Dedicated runtime — it's optimized kernels, batching, quantization paths. For teams that want to keep vLLM we can route traffic with a hybrid policy or provide a side-by-side comparison. Important bit is model artifact compatibility — we ask for your checkpoint + tokenizer so we can validate.
[02:14] Marcus: And quantization? We're on 4-bit quant in vLLM for cost — will Redwood support that?
[02:19] Jonah: Yes, we have quantization-friendly execution, most common 4-bit/8-bit profiles. We'll check your specific format; sometimes conversion needed (weights layout, fused kernels). We'll include conversion notes in the benchmark pack.
[02:34] Priya: Security questions: Can you outline data handling for Dedicated vs Private? We need audit logs, KMS key control, SSO, and proof of SOC2.
[02:43] Maya: For Dedicated you get tenant isolation and audit logs; keys can be customer-managed via KMS integrations. Private gives you control-plane in your VPC and options for on-prem. We'll send SOC2 and ISO docs and a diagram of data flow.
[02:58] Priya: What about retention and egress? Our legal wants a min retention and contract clause for not using prompts to train models.
[03:06] Maya: Redwood doesn't use customer prompts for training. Retention policies are configurable; we'll share the legal checklist.
[03:12] Alex: On performance — our SLAs: sub-200ms tail latency for single-shot generation up to 512 tokens. We're worried about batching affecting P50/P95.
[03:22] Jonah: We can tune batching policies per route to meet latency SLOs; Dedicated can guarantee throughput with reserved GPU capacity. We'll run an A/B with your traffic profile. Also prefix/KV caching often helps for repeated contexts.
[03:36] Marcus: For eval parity, what's the recommended test suite? We have a sparkle of prompts: 10k evals, mix of long and short contexts, function calls.
transcript_continued:
[03:44] Jonah: We'll provide a benchmark checklist: token distribution, sequence length histogram, sample prompt set (function calls included), and expected output hashes where possible. For function-calling we test both structured output and tool-calling behavior.
[03:58] Lena: Any gotchas about tokenizer differences — we saw earlier that stop sequences sometimes behave differently moving between OpenAI and our local runs.
[04:06] Jonah: Right. Tokenizer mismatches are common; we'll first align on tokenizer (shared vocab/file). If you have a custom pre-tokenization step we'll reproduce it. Also sampling seeds are different, so exact string equality isn't always feasible; we look at semantic equivalence and eval metrics.
[04:25] Marcus: Timeline: ideally pilot in next week or two; production migration Q4.
[04:30] Maya: That fits — we can aim to kick a 1-week pilot week of 2026-10-27. Pilot scope: run your 10k evals, latency benchmarks, and a small live canary.
[04:41] Priya: For the pilot we need a security questionnaire answered and our compliance team in the loop.
[04:46] Maya: We'll send the security questionnaire and SOC2/ISO docs. Jonah will also include the conversion checklist for vLLM/TGI artifacts.
[04:54] Alex: Pricing — can you give rough numbers? OpenAI costs us a lot at 1B tokens/month.
[05:00] Maya: We'll send a TCO model — reserved Dedicated pricing vs hosted per-token. For 1B tokens we usually show 30-50% reduction with a committed Dedicated pool depending on model and quantization. Exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:13] Marcus: Do you support running custom kernels / FPGA? We use specific optimizations in vLLM stack.
[05:18] Jonah: We don't expose custom kernel uploads for hosted Dedicated but we support common fused kernels and kernel selection at runtime. For Private/on-prem we can discuss deeper integration with your infra.
[05:30] Lena: What's the rollback story if we see quality regression?
[05:34] Jonah: We do canary rollouts, A/B testing and immediate fallback to your prior variant (OpenAI or vLLM) via routing policies until you sign off. We'll keep both models for a short window.
[05:45] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps...
[05:48] Maya: We'll send pricing/TCO, SOC2/ISO, security questionnaire, and the benchmark pack. Jonah will help onboard artifacts and run the initial benchmark. Iris to share prompts and token hist by 10/25. Pilot kickoff targeted 10/27.
[06:05] Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:07] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the deck and links.
[06:11] (call ends)
